resources.string: Pure Kotlin core. Lines only — no fills or double outlines.
See the real pipeline turn a letter image into lines for a pen. This is a development tool, not the finished application.
Original synthetic PNGs · 300 × 300 · 6 px strokes. Not real handwriting.
PNG / JPEG · up to 5 MB and 1 million pixels. Not a full page yet: recognition and text segmentation are not implemented.
This browser sandbox sends the image to a test server. Do not upload private pages. The server processes bytes in memory without saving images to disk.
I understand that this test image will be sent to the sandbox
Each color is a separate graph chain
Time inside vectorize, excluding PNG decoding, network and SVG serialization
Natural letter loops are preserved. Zero closed polylines does not mean their loops were removed.
Parameters go to the real PipelineParams. The browser does not implement the mathematics.
SVG is for inspecting lines. Alphabet .gfont export is not implemented yet.
M1 processes one cropped letter. Notebook capture, character recognition, alphabet storage and .gfont are later milestones. KDraw will own cross-set missing-character substitution.
Ж splits into 8 chains instead of 3 authored lines. Diagonals are still jagged. Junction cleanup and smoothing are needed; perfect handwriting is not claimed.

Images and metrics are generated from the current :core by the server. Personal alphabet files require further Android development.
Import an image. Prepare it for processing.
A notebook page or drawing: rotation, crop, four corners, rectification and B/W use the real Kotlin core. Character recognition and drawing outlines are not implemented yet.
Drag the four green corners. Filled handles are UI markers, not result outlines.
When disabled, dimensions follow the frame edges without guessing millimeters. Arbitrary drawings do not require A4.
Prepared pixels, not recognized letters or SVG outlines.
Added to the plan: drawing → outlines

A separate mode will turn drawings into outline paths: SVG/PNG downloads, SVG copy and file sharing. It will not replace handwriting centerlines. Outlines are not implemented yet; M2 builds shared input.
The detector looks for bright paper on a darker background. Repair the frame manually on complex or low-contrast backgrounds. A synthetic test does not prove behavior on every photograph.
No confident corners found — use the manual frame.
M2: preparation. M3: recognition needs its own design. Drawing outlines and their file actions are separately planned M6 scope.
